story: UPDATE to No.61. The University of Alaska's learning rule for AI, read through UAA's first public AI misconduct count, ahead of the regents' November principles in Fairbanks
stories_surviving: A: University of Alaska AI rules for learning and the UAA AI misconduct count (update)
B: Hilcorp Beluga River gas storage, Corps emergency processing (runner-up)

claims.claim: UAA's Dean of Students Office report counted 150 students cited for academic misconduct.
claims.verbatim: Of the 150 students cited for academic misconduct, 119 used AI, accounting for 1.1% of the more than 10,500 students who attended UAA last semester.
claims.notes: The report itself was not published; attribute as the report described by ADN. 'Cited' differs from 2025's 'found responsible'.

claims.claim: Of the students cited for academic misconduct at UAA, 119 used AI.
claims.verbatim: Of the 150 students cited for academic misconduct, 119 used AI

claims.claim: The 119 AI cases equal 1.1% of the more than 10,500 students who attended UAA last semester.
claims.verbatim: accounting for 1.1% of the more than 10,500 students who attended UAA last semester
claims.notes: Do not compare the 10,500 base with 2025's 8,800 as growth.

claims.claim: The report shows a 73% increase in AI use for plagiarism last year.
claims.verbatim: The report shows a 73% increase in AI use for plagiarism last year and a 56% increase in academic misconduct overall.
claims.notes: Attribute to the report and never recompute.

claims.claim: The report shows a 56% increase in academic misconduct overall.
claims.verbatim: a 56% increase in academic misconduct overall

claims.claim: The UAA report on generative AI use among students was produced with assistance from generative AI tools.
claims.value: with assistance from generative AI tools
claims.verbatim: with assistance from generative AI tools
claims.notes: Source sentence carries dashes; fragment only.

claims.claim: The Dean of Students Office released the report in August.
claims.verbatim: by the Dean of Students Office and released in August

claims.claim: The report states that cases involving AI use now make up the majority of cases handled by the UAA conduct office.
claims.verbatim: Cases involving AI use have taken over the majority of cases addressed by the conduct office.

claims.claim: The UA system has no single policy governing AI use across more than a dozen campuses.
claims.verbatim: The UA system does not have a single policy governing AI use across more than a dozen individual campuses.

claims.claim: Current UAA guidance lets professors tailor their syllabi to allow as much or as little AI use as they like.
claims.value: as much or as little AI usage
claims.verbatim: The current guidance allows professors to tailor their syllabi to allow as much or as little AI usage in class as they like

claims.claim: The UAA Faculty Senate specifically requested the current faculty-by-faculty structure.
claims.verbatim: The UAA Faculty Senate specifically requested the current structure.

claims.claim: UAA spokesperson Catalina Myers said letting faculty decide AI use preserved the integrity of academic freedom.
claims.verbatim: "Allowing faculty to determine appropriate AI use in their classrooms was preferable to a single blanket policy because it preserved the integrity of academic freedom,

claims.claim: The report said UAA requires all faculty to address AI use in their syllabus.
claims.verbatim: The report also said UAA requires all faculty to address AI use in their syllabus, but discourages the use of AI checkers.

claims.claim: UAA discourages the use of AI checkers, according to the report.
claims.value: discourages the use of AI checkers
claims.verbatim: but discourages the use of AI checkers

claims.claim: UAA associate professor Andrew Harnish said many faculty use AI checkers in practice.
claims.verbatim: Andrew Harnish, an associate professor in UAA's writing department, said that in practice, many faculty use AI checkers to see if their students have turned in work generated by a chatbot

claims.claim: UA regents are scheduled to consider guiding principles for integrating AI throughout the UA system in November.
claims.verbatim: Regents will consider guiding principles for integrating AI throughout the UA system in November.

claims.claim: Special projects lead Stephanie Erickson presented the draft language to regents in September alongside Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier.
claims.verbatim: Stephanie Erickson, a special projects lead who presented the draft language to regents in September alongside Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier

claims.claim: Erickson told regents the university needs to be deliberate about engaging with AI instead of letting it just happen.
claims.verbatim: "We need to be deliberate with how we want to engage with AI instead of letting it just happen to us," Erickson said.

claims.claim: The draft document calls for "appropriate AI in every discipline" and says humans must remain "in the loop."
claims.verbatim: calls for "appropriate AI in every discipline" and emphasizes that humans must remain "in the loop."

claims.claim: Erickson said being in the loop means AI could recommend but a human decides.
claims.verbatim: So 'in the loop' means that AI could recommend but a human decides.
claims.notes: Quote only the words AI could recommend but a human decides.

claims.claim: Erickson also said AI can't act alone.
claims.verbatim: AI cannot act alone.

claims.claim: Shier drafted the AI intent language over the summer at the request of regents.
claims.verbatim: Shier drafted the AI intent language over the summer at the request of regents.

claims.claim: Feedback from staff and students on the draft was included but limited, according to Shier.
claims.verbatim: Feedback from staff and students was included, but limited, according to Shier, who said the document is meant as a broad overview.

claims.claim: Shier called AI one of the most profound technology shifts the university has ever seen.
claims.verbatim: "This, in my mind, is one of the most profound technology shifts that we have ever seen."

claims.claim: UAA sophomore and student government member Brigitta Taaga pushed back on the draft language as not going far enough.
claims.verbatim: pushed back against the language, claiming it didn't go far enough.
claims.notes: ADN paraphrase, not her quoted words.

claims.claim: Taaga said most of the younger generations are really against AI.
claims.verbatim: "Most of the younger generations are really against it," Taaga said.

claims.claim: Non-traditional UAA student Michael Feign said the draft offers overarching ideas rather than nitty-gritty policy.
claims.verbatim: "What they present is a lot of overarching ideas and not really like nitty-gritty policy," Feign said.

claims.claim: Feign said he would prefer the university build its own large language model hosted on local servers.
claims.verbatim: Feign said he would prefer the university protect student data by building its own large language model hosted on local servers.

claims.claim: UAA vice chancellor Aaron Dotson said there is no instruction manual.
claims.verbatim: "There is no instruction manual," Dotson said.

claims.claim: A year earlier, a Dean of Students Office report showed 115 UAA students were found responsible for academic misconduct.
claims.verbatim: Of the more than 8,800 UAA students, a report from the Dean of Students Office showed that 115 were found responsible for academic misconduct last year.
claims.notes: 'Found responsible', not 'cited'; never present 115 to 150 as a rise.

claims.claim: About two-thirds of those 115 cases were AI-related.
claims.verbatim: Of those, about two-thirds of cases were AI-related.
claims.notes: Never convert to a case count.

claims.claim: UAA's conduct code addresses AI use through the section prohibiting "utilizing devices not authorized by faculty members."
claims.value: devices not authorized by faculty members
claims.verbatim: a section of the student code of conduct that prohibits "utilizing devices not authorized by faculty members."
claims.notes: Per Michael Votava, assistant dean of students and director of student conduct and ethical development; the 2026 ADN article quotes the same handbook phrase.

claims.claim: A UAA professor hid a nearly invisible prompt in an assignment, and AI chatbots that six students pasted the problem into saw it.
claims.verbatim: Students who completed their own work did not see the "Trojan horse." But AI chatbots that six students pasted the problem into did
claims.notes: Hidden in light-colored ink and a small font.

claims.claim: UAA issues suspensions for academic dishonesty only about once every two years.
claims.verbatim: suspensions for academic dishonesty are only issued about once every two years
claims.notes: Most students caught complete an academic integrity tutorial and may get a written warning.

claims.claim: The UA Board of Regents calendar lists BOR Committee Meetings beginning at 1 p.m. Alaska time on November 4th.
claims.verbatim: DTSTART:20261104T220000Z DTEND:20261105T020000Z SUMMARY:BOR Committee Meetings
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Board of Regents public calendar
claims.notes: 22:00 UTC is 1 p.m. AKST. Calendar embedded at https://www.alaska.edu/bor/schedules/index.php.

claims.claim: The regents calendar lists a Committee and Full Board Meeting in Fairbanks on November 5th.
claims.verbatim: DTSTART:20261105T170000Z DTEND:20261106T020000Z SUMMARY:Committee/Full Board Meeting in Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Board of Regents public calendar

claims.claim: The regents calendar lists the Board of Regents' Meeting in Fairbanks on November 6th.
claims.verbatim: DTSTART:20261106T170000Z DTEND:20261107T020000Z SUMMARY:Board of Regents' Meeting in Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Board of Regents public calendar

claims.claim: The regents calendar lists a Public Testimony session from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. Alaska time on Monday, November 2nd.
claims.verbatim: DTSTART:20261103T010000Z DTEND:20261103T020000Z SUMMARY:Public Testimony
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Board of Regents public calendar
claims.notes: UTC stamps; Alaska is on AKST (UTC minus 9) after November 1st, so 01:00Z November 3rd is 4 p.m. November 2nd. Showrunner read the raw ICS by curl.

claims.claim: KTOO reported that the draft AI policy would require all three UA universities to have a plan to address AI.
claims.verbatim: The University of Alaska's draft artificial intelligence policy would require all three of its campuses to have a plan in place to address artificial intelligence, like ChatGPT.
claims.notes: Three universities versus ADN's more than a dozen campuses.

claims.claim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.verbatim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.

claims.claim: About 85% of college students use generative AI in their coursework, according to a 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey cited by KTOO.
claims.verbatim: It finds that about 85% of college students use generative AI in their coursework.

claims.claim: The UA Statewide AI Symposium ran September 25th to 27th at the ConocoPhillips Integrated Science Building in Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: September 25 - September 27 ... ConocoPhillips Integrated Science Building

claims.claim: The symposium closed with a strategy session for the UA statewide AI advisory council.
claims.verbatim: Sunday will close with a strategy session for the UA statewide AI advisory council.

claims.claim: UA's Systemwide AI in Communications Guidelines were developed over five months.
claims.verbatim: developed over five months by a cross-functional working group of communications professionals from across the UA system

claims.claim: The communications guidelines don't address classroom, instructional or research uses of AI.
claims.verbatim: They do not address classroom, instructional or research uses of AI.

claims.claim: UA's Generative AI Security Standard took effect in January 2025 and governs data and tool procurement rather than academic integrity.
claims.verbatim: Effective Date: January 2025
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology

claims.claim: The Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District issued a September 29th public notice processing a Hilcorp Beluga gas storage permit on an emergency basis.
claims.verbatim: In a Sept. 29 public notice the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District said it is processing a permit application from Hilcorp Alaska for work related to natural gas storage at Beluga

claims.claim: Comments on the Corps notice are due by October 30th, according to Petroleum News.
claims.verbatim: Comments are due by Oct. 30.

claims.claim: The proposed Beluga gas storage pad would cover some 7.38 acres.
claims.verbatim: some 7.38 acres with some 2.35 acres of palustrine wetlands directly filled

claims.claim: The pad would directly fill some 2.35 acres of palustrine wetlands.
claims.verbatim: some 7.38 acres with some 2.35 acres of palustrine wetlands directly filled

claims.claim: DNR noticed Hilcorp's application for a Beluga River gas storage lease covering approximately 6,100 acres of state-owned subsurface reservoir.
claims.verbatim: Approximately 6,100 acres of State-owned subsurface gas storage reservoir
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Story B background; comment period closed July 8th.

killed.claim: The regents' Public Testimony session is on November 3rd.
killed.why: The ICS stamp is UTC; in Alaska it is 4 p.m. November 2nd. Kept as C38 with the Alaska date.

killed.claim: AI chatbots that six students used produced different answers to the hidden prompt.
killed.why: The page says the chatbots saw the hidden prompt. Restated as C33.

killed.claim: Erickson said, as one continuous quote, AI could recommend but a human decides. AI cannot act alone.
killed.why: Adjacency unconfirmed across fetches; kept separately as C20 and C21.

killed.claim: Taaga said the draft 'didn't go far enough' in her own words.
killed.why: ADN paraphrase; kept unquoted as C25.

killed.claim: UAA AI misconduct rose from 115 cases to 150 cases.
killed.why: Different measures (found responsible versus cited) and bases; use only the report's own 73% and 56%, attributed.

killed.claim: The DNR Beluga gas storage lease comment period is open.
Hilcorp filed its AOGCC storage injection order application by September 1st.
killed.why: Petroleum News says only that Hilcorp intended to.
